title: Publishing an image needs a workflow; there is no way to push one by hand
foundBy: user (host), while settling the publish design: "no cs-sandbox push for now, add a ledger entry for it as an idea"
details:
CI is the only publisher of the sandbox images. It builds them from a clean checkout of a pushed commit and pushes them to `ghcr.io/codesweep-ai/sandbox` and the two `-slim` packages, which is what makes a tag mean "the image CI built from this commit".

That leaves no supported way for a maintainer to publish one from a workstation. The cases where it would matter are narrow: a workflow that is broken, a registry outage that dropped a tag, or a one-off image for a revision CI skipped. `podman push` does the job today, because `cs-sandbox build` already tags the fully-qualified name that a push takes unaltered.

A `cs-sandbox push` would add the checks a bare `podman push` has no way to make: refuse a `-dirty` tag, refuse a revision the module proxy cannot resolve, and refuse an image whose `cs-sandbox` came from `--local-sandbox` rather than from the version its tag names. Each of those publishes something the tag misdescribes.

Worth doing only if hand-publishing turns out to be a thing that happens. Until then the absence is deliberate, and this record is here so the reason is findable.
